item.title: Five Shows to See in New York City Right Now
item.description: Three millennia of storytelling at the Morgan, Goya’s visions of war, Alison Nguyen’s diasporic tale, and Indigenous artistry in every medium imaginable.

item.title: Bad Bunny’s “Benito Bowl” Enters the Meme Canon
item.description: The half-time show tribute to Boricua and Latine pride was rife with cultural and political symbolism that resonated with millions.

item.title: Bad Bunny Makes Meme History
item.description: How the "Benito Bowl" took on a second life in the digital realm, Israel's artwashing at the Venice Biennale, an art history of liminalism, and shows to see in NYC.

item.title: The Biennale Certificate in Philosophy and Art
item.description: The Institute for Doctoral Studies in the Visual Arts (IDSVA) invites creatives from all backgrounds to apply for this four-day summer program in Venice.

item.title: These Are the Artists in MoMA PS1’s Greater New York Show
item.description: On its 50th anniversary year, the Queens-based museum tapped 53 local artists for the sixth edition of its cross-borough survey.

item.title: Beer With a Painter: Mary Lovelace O'Neal
item.description: “At this marvelous hard-won age, the days of jumping and dancing with the paintings are over. But I don't feel limited,” says the artist, educator, and Civil Rights luminary.

item.title: Art and Power Collide in New York City
item.description: The Epstein files rip through the art world's elite, yet hope emerges in the work of Goya, Amazonian artists, and three millennia of storytellers.

item.title: Amanda Ross-Ho Finds Herself in Her Parents' Art
item.description: The artist's current show is a moving reflection on the ways our identities are inexorably entangled with our relationships and surroundings.

item.title: Pride Flag Removed From Stonewall Monument at Trump’s Directive
item.description: The move comes a year after the National Park Service scrubbed mentions of queer and trans people from its website, prompting protests at the NYC landmark.

item.title: 10 Art Shows to See in the Bay Area This Spring
item.description: Theresa Hak Kyung Cha’s vital scrolls, muralist Cece Carpio’s first solo show, the Matisse painting that launched Fauvism, the future of Japanese ceramic art, and more.
